nearest_prs.title: Lever a paint tin's lid off with a screwdriver
nearest_prs.why_close: Same core skill: one arm picks up a flat screwdriver and levers an object out against a rim/ledge fulcrum, the other arm turns the workpiece between pries because one side only is reachable.

nearest_prs.title: Pry a nailed 1x4 off two joists with a flat bar, levering on each joist in turn
nearest_prs.why_close: Alternating pry points with a lever tool to free a held part evenly.

nearest_prs.title: Core a whole apple with a tube corer
nearest_prs.why_close: Removing a cut plug from a tube; different skill (cutting).

physical_skill: Lever a press-fit plug axially out of a slotted cup with a flat screwdriver on a ledge fulcrum, turning the cup half a turn between pries so pries alternate sides (one-sided pries wedge it).
valid_shortcuts: None found that score >0 without prying; one-arm and no-turn routes score 0.0 and 0.25.
distinct_from_nearest: Not clearly distinct. Differences from #922 (alternating sides to avoid wedging, choosing the low or high slot step) are refinements of the same screwdriver-lever-and-turn-between-pries skill on a different object; REVIEW_BAR says a different body alone does not establish a new skill, and CODEX.md's manual round already killed the hole-saw core concept. Not submitted; Dream-1 not spent.
